label: text
text: FERRIER AND BUDD.

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: Shanghai, November'2.

label: text
text: The amateur got championship of China over seventy-two holes, on Saturday and Sunday, resulted in a tie between J. B. Ferrier (last year's champion) and M. W. Budd. Ferrier at end of the first day led by 7 strokes, scoring 75 and 74. Budd was fourth with 83 and 77. On Sunday morning Ferrier and Budd each scored 73.

label: text
text: In the afternoon Ferrier returned 83 and Budd 72.

label: text
text: An eighteen hole deciding match will be played on Tuesday.

text: EGYPTIAN DECREE.

label: paragraph_title
text: SAFEGUARDING PUBLIC SECURITY

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Pilmy Pasha Issa, Minister of the Interior has stated that the subjected of Political Organisations Law was to safeguard public security, eliminate harmful societies, and to organise the political life of the country.

label: text
text: There was no intention whatever to interfere with the rightful liberty of the people. All must obey the law, but requests for delay in regard to complying therewith would be generously considered.

label: text
text: "Consternation has been created by the royal decree compelling all political organisations to make declaration with regard to their headquarters and membership within a month."

label: text
text: A prominent politician speaking to Reuter declared it was a most reactionary step, likely to have the gravest results, and leading to the reappearance of secret societies.

label: text
text: He had reason to believe that the Zaghulists, Liberals and Watanists, will ignore the decree and defy the Government.

HOOVER AND BRITISH
RESTRICTION.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: New York, November 1. Mr. Hoover said that up to October last year, the controllers of East Indies rubber had uniformly declared that the industry sought only between 30 and 55 cents per pound. Our investigation showed that they earned 25 per cent upon invested capital. At that price today it is over $1 per lb, yet the production is restricted. Now it is said it must recoup growers previous losses.

label: paragraph_title
text: SEAPLANE'S FALL.

label: text
text: NARROW ESCAPE FROM DEATH.

label: text
text: AVIATORS' EXPERIENCE

label: text
text: Lieut. Mackintosh and Flying Officer Phillips, the two officers in the seaplane which crashed into the harbour off West Point early yesterday morning were both injured, one but slightly, the other sustaining injuries to his back.

label: text
text: Dragging operations which have been proceeding since shortly after the accident have resulted in the recovery of most parts of the plane although after its submersion and the effects of the fall from a height of from 800 to 1,000 feet it is not thought that anything other than the engine will be of much use.

label: text
text: At the time of the accident the seaplane with two others, all of the bombing type, were returning from escorting the s.s. "Kalyan" on which was the new Governor of Hongkong. His Excellency Mr. Cecil Clementi, C.M.G., and by some means or other two of the planes changed their relative positions with the result that the plane on which were the two officers mentioned got underneath and near to the other. The effect on the elements of a plane's passage is naturally at its strongest underneath, a not inapt comparison being that of the wake of a ship. The inevitable consequence of the change of positions was that the former plane side slipped and fell.

label: text
text: At the time the water was reached control had almost been regained by the pilot, the plane being almost righted after its vertical drop. The water was struck with terrific impact and a huge wave swept the decks of the s.s. "Tean" between which and the "Ninghai" the plane fell with not a lot of distance between each.

label: text
text: As communication by wireless when the 'planes are out of sight and by observation otherwise is always kept with H.M.S. "Hermes," the accident was noted aboard and a ship's pinnace and police launch were soon on the spot. Both officers were found to have freed themselves from their trappings, the emergency accomplishment of which can be achieved in one action. They both kept afloat and when the pinnace and launch arrived were found to be safe in sampans. They were conveyed to H.M.S. "Hermes."

label: paragraph_title
text: MR. AHMEDBHOY CURRIMBHOY.

label: text
text: A cable from Bombay to Hongkong brought the news yesterday of the death of Mr. Ahmedbhoy Currimbhoy, connected with the firm of Currimbhoy & Co., Wyndham Street, Hongkong, and his many friends found chiefly among the Mohammedan community heard of it with deep regret.

label: text
text: A telegram of condolence from the Mohammedan community of Hongkong was sent to the relatives of the deceased and a ceremony was carried out at the Mosque in this Colony.

label: text
text: Deceased was a son of the late Sir Currimbhoy Ebrahim, Bart.

text: The final state of parties is likely to be 116 conservatives, 102 Liberals, 22 Progressive, two Labour and two Independents. Probably the Prime Minister, Mr. Mackenzie King will await a possible defeat in Parliament and then resign and re-omniend new elections to clear up the stalemate.

label: text

label: text
text: That the entry of the Canton "Red" troops into Swatow was imminent was the first of a message received by the Naval authorities this morning.

label: text
text: Beyond this no subsequent advice has arrived stating that Swatow had actually fallen but on the face of the intelligence, and in view of events during the weekend, it is more than a presumption that only a miracle can save the last—and the most important—base for the anti-Reds, under General Chan Kwing-ming.

label: text
text: Information from other sources has been very meagre. From one reliable quarter it was gathered that the anti-Red centre which had inflicted a defeat in the field, not far from Swatow, had become disintegrated, letting in the Reds through the salient in the line.

label: text
text: General Li Tik-piu's army is stated to have failed to join the counter-offensive at the height of that last anti-Red victory. When the Reds came back all the territory gained was sacrificed, the anti-Red morale being badly shaken.

text:

text: “DOING WELL.”

label: text
text: MR. JENKIN RECOVERING FROM INJURIES.

label: text
text: SATURDAY'S ACCIDENT:

label: text
text: Friends of My T. Jenkin, of Messrs. Leisland Orange, will be pleased to hear that this gentle-man is overlying from an accident which necessitated his removal to the Government Civil Hospital. On inquiry this morning it was ascertained that he was doing well.

label: text
text: As stated in the "China Mail" on Saturday, Mr. Jenkin was thrown out of a ricsha. on to the pavement of the Astor House Hotel; sustaining a big wound in the head, which rendered him unconscious. The accident occurred at a time when there were few people about the street owing to the departure of the Governor, and the ricsha coolie took the opportunity to make a bolt. The number of the vehicle has, however, been ascertained by Detective Sub-Inspector Fallon, and the traffic department are making inquiries.

label: text
text: A Chinese named Cheung Ting, 24, was charged before Mr. S. B. B. McElderry at the Central Magistracy this morning with driving a car while his licence had been suspended.

label: text
text: His Worship was informed that the defendant was fined $25 on Saturday for the same offence and he was caught in the act again yesterday.

label: text
text:
A fine of $50 was imposed.
Another Chinese employed by the P.W.D. as a steam lorry driver was charged with driving a motor cycle in Li Tung Street without a proper licence.

label: text
text: It was stated by a traffic official that the defendant was driving in a dangerous manner and had no proper control over his machine. Defendant was fined $25.

label: paragraph_title

MOTOR MISHAPS.
TWO PEDESTRIANS
INJURED.

label: text
text:
A Chinese woman was injured near the Wanchai market yesterday afternoon when she walked in front of a motor car and was dragged for some distance along the road. She was picked up in an unconscious condition.
Lance-Corporal Meaker, of Murray Barracks, who was driving the car, immediately conveyed the woman to the Government Civil Hospital and reported the incident later.
At Wanchai Road or Saturday morning a Chinese boy was injured in the forehead and legs when he walked in front of a motor cycle driven by Sergeant Baunders.

Having thus taken his place in the revolutionary world before reaching manhood, Frunze was chosen in 1906, at the age of 21, to attend the Stockholm conference of the Social Democratic Party as delegate of the Bolsheviks.
Later he went to work in the textile mills at Ivanovovoannenskä, a manufacturing town in central Russia, where he was arrested on a charge or organising a Social Democratic Union. He was also accused of resisting the police who are rested him. He came before the courts five times and was twice sentenced to death. Though he escaped execution, he was sent to the Siberian mines to serve a sentence of ten years' hard labour. He was there when the war broke out, but in 1915 he escaped and was able to conduct revolutionary propaganda in the Tear's army, apparently without detection.
After Kerensky's revolution in February, 1917, he took part in the struggles against Kornilo, who organised a counter-revolt. He was also active in organising sovjets in the army in White Russia. When the Bolshevik revolution came in the following November he became chairman of the executive committee of the Government and Military Commissary in Ivanovovoannenskä. Afterwards he became Commander-in-Chief of four armies in the south-east, where the advantage of Admiral Kolchak's forces was stopped. He was again successful in the operations against the White armies in Turkestan. In 1920 he took command of the operations against Global Wrangel.
